findings.title: `Stop()` no longer rejects requests after the per-RPC `Init` guards were removed
findings.description: `Stop()` sets `s.initErr` to "service is stopping" / "service is stopped". Before this diff every RPC began with `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil { return nil, err }`, so those values made a stopped server refuse work. All of those guards are gone and the only remaining caller of `Init` is `NewResourceServer` (server.go:258). The `initErr` writes in `Stop()` are now dead state, and Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch run against a backend whose lifecycle `Stop` has already been called. Either add an explicit stopped check (e.g. an atomic flag or `s.ctx.Err()`) or remove the dead assignments and document that the gRPC layer must drain first.

findings.title: New `TotalDocs()` call reads the bleve cache map without a lock while the event goroutine can write it
findings.description: The diff adds `s.search.TotalDocs()` to the init log line at pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216. `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu`. That line runs after the event goroutine is started at search.go:207-213, and that goroutine can reach `BuildIndex`, which writes `b.cache[key]` (bleve.go:137-139). A concurrent map iteration and write is a fatal runtime error in Go, not a recoverable panic. The same unlocked read is already reachable from the metrics collector (bleve_index_metrics.go:96). Since this diff reworks `cacheMu` usage in the same file, take `b.cacheMu.RLock()` in `TotalDocs`.

findings.title: Postgres run of the storage-server integration test is skipped rather than fixed
findings.description: `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` starts the `StorageServer` target, which runs `service.start` → `sql.NewResourceServer` → `resource.NewResourceServer`. That is exactly the path this diff changes to initialise eagerly. The test is now skipped for postgres with "not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally." and a TODO with no issue reference. With sqlite already skipped, only MySQL covers the path. A test that starts failing in CI alongside a startup-ordering change is evidence of a regression or timing dependency: the test relies on a fixed 500 ms sleep at line 56, and startup now does DB init and index build synchronously. No tests were added for eager init, the init order, or the `BuildIndex` locking change.

findings.title: Shared `err` and counter are written from concurrent errgroup workers in `searchSupport.init`
findings.description: This predates the diff, but it sits in the function the diff modifies. Each `group.Go` closure assigns to the outer `err` (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increments `totalBatchesIndexed` with no synchronisation. With `initWorkers > 1`, one worker's failure can be overwritten by another's `nil` before `return err` executes. That swallows an index-build error which the function comment says must block startup. Removing the global lock in `BuildIndex` means builds now genuinely overlap, widening the window. Use a closure-local `err` and an atomic counter (or use `len(stats)`).

findings.title: Removing the `BuildIndex` lock lets same-key builds run in parallel
findings.description: Narrowing `cacheMu` to the map write is right for letting `WorkerThreads` do something. But `getOrCreateIndex` (pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:287-307) is check-then-act with no per-key guard, as its own TODO admits. Two concurrent searches, or a search and a watch event, for an uncached key both build an index. The last writer wins in `b.cache`, the loser is never closed, and writes to it are lost. `IndexTenants` and `IndexedKinds` are also double-counted. Previously these duplicate builds ran one after another; now they overlap, including a possible concurrent `bleve.New(dir, …)` on the same directory for file-backed indexes. Re-checking the cache under the lock, or a per-key `singleflight`, would close this.

findings.title: Failure path of eager `Init` leaks resources and logs the error twice
findings.description: If `s.Init(ctx)` fails, `NewResourceServer` returns without calling `cancel()` or `s.lifecycle.Stop`. A backend whose DB was opened in `lifecycle.Init` is therefore left running, along with any poller or watch goroutine started by `search.init`. The same error is logged with the same message at line 314 inside `Init` and again at line 260.

findings.title: Eager init uses the server's internal context and blocks construction
findings.description: `Init` runs with the long-lived "watcher" service-account context built at lines 229-235. Callers such as `sql.NewResourceServer(ctx, …)` (pkg/storage/unified/sql/server.go:77) cannot cancel or bound startup, and the `unified_search.Init` span has no parent. The whole index build now also runs synchronously inside the constructor, including the dependency-injection-time path in pkg/storage/unified/client.go:101. That matches the "any failure will block startup" intent but deserves a comment on `NewResourceServer`.

findings.title: Tracing context propagation and logger fix
findings.description: Replacing `_, span :=` with `ctx, span :=` in `searchSupport.init` (search.go:173), `searchSupport.build` (search.go:310) and `backend.GetResourceStats` (pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go:126) correctly parents downstream spans. In each case the derived `ctx` is used afterwards (`GetResourceStats`, `builders.get`/`ListIterator`, `db.WithTx`). Swapping the `grafana-cli` `logger.Warn` for `s.log.Warn` at search.go:280 removes an inappropriate CLI-package dependency from the storage layer.

findings.title: Init ordering: search index before watcher
findings.description: Building the search index before `initWatcher()` is consistent with the eager-init design. `initWatcher` uses only `s.ctx` and `s.backend`, and the lifecycle hook still runs first, so the reorder introduces no dependency problem.
